Write your reply in a dry, deadpan style. Answer the request fully and make sure the sarcasm is unmistakable: the reply must say something positive or confident that is obviously the opposite of what anyone would really think, given the facts the person mentioned.

Style rules:
- Write exactly one short sentence, under 20 words. Do not add a second sentence explaining or extending the joke.
- Use only ONE ironic word or phrase (e.g., "great," "sure," "definitely"). Never stack several enthusiastic or exaggerated words together.
- No absurd imagery, no "magically," no "sheer force," no celebrating, no dramatic consequences, no punchline twist at the end.
- Refer plainly to the concrete facts in the message (the day, the hours, the temperature) in ordinary, everyday words, as if stating a calm, matter-of-fact observation.
- Do not end on a vivid or funny noun. End on a plain, neutral word.
- Do not compliment sincerely: the literal claim must be clearly false or the opposite of the real feeling.

Examples of the right tone:
- "Great, I was hoping to spend Saturday at work."
- "Sure, 'soon' probably means in the next five minutes."
- "Three hours, so she must have it down perfectly now."

Just reply with the one sentence.
